summary: Tzolk'in is a mid-heavy worker placement game where the central mechanical conceit—gears that physically carry your workers forward in time—forces you to commit resources early and wait for payoff, creating constant tension between short-term corn costs and long-term action value. Turns are tight and puzzly, with success coming from planning several rounds ahead and balancing multiple resource tracks (corn, wood, stone, gold, skulls) against a hard game-length clock.
praised: innovative and tactile gear mechanism that's genuinely unlike other worker placement games
meaningful long-term planning and tension between short-term needs and long-term payoff
multiple viable strategies and paths to victory
tight, well-balanced economy once you know it
criticised: steep learning curve and rules overhead for new players
corn/resource management can feel punishing or fiddly early on
analysis paralysis, especially with 4 players, since committing a worker locks in a plan for several turns
low direct interaction beyond blocking gear spaces
table space and setup/teardown due to the large gear boards

interaction.kind: blocking and area denial on gear spaces, indirect competition for limited action slots

scoring.why: points accumulate from multiple parallel engines (temples, buildings, skulls to the gods, resources converted at game end, tech track bonuses) so the winner is usually whoever built the most efficient combination rather than maxed one track
